entities.summary: Abram Lincoln Harris Jr. was an American economist, academic, anthropologist and a social critic of the condition of black people in the United States. He was considered by many as the first African American to achieve prominence in the field of economics. He was also known for his heavy influence on black radical and neo-conservative thought in the United States. As an economist, Harris is most famous for his 1931 collaboration with political scientist Sterling Spero to produce a study on African-American labor history titled The Black Worker and his 1936 work The Negro as Capitalist, in which he criticized black businessmen for not promoting interracial trade.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Harris's work on African-American labor history and his critique of black businessmen for not promoting interracial trade had a significant impact on the Civil Rights Movement in the United States. His research influenced prominent figures such as W.E.B. Du Bois and Langston Hughes.
